notes:
Lead source: webinar signups -> content ops track. Product: Fluxscribe offers a multi-tenant content generation API used by ~120 publishers and agencies. Primary ask: reduce per-output cost while maintaining response quality for short-form marketing copy (subject lines, ad copy, landing page variants). They generate high volumes with traffic spikes at campaign launches (typical baseline 2M tokens/mo, spikes to ~10M tokens). Interested in hosted API for fastest time-to-value; not ready for Dedicated. Key priorities: unit economics, predictable QoS during spikes, caching/prefix reuse across campaigns, easy SDKs and streaming for UI. Quote from CTO: "We need predictable billing when we push huge campaign blasts — can't have surprise bills."

CRM-style notes (shorthand):
- POC ask: 2-day smoke with 3 campaign patterns (subject lines, body variants, ad copy). Use cheap open-model baseline + recommended Redwood model for quality check.
- Latency target: median generation <400ms for 32-token outputs, 95th <900ms during bursts.
- Throughput: need ability to handle ~300 req/s at peak (batched), prefer continuous batching + KV prefix cache.
- Cost sensitivity: want guidance on batching window, token vs request tradeoffs, recommended quantized models for selected tasks.
- Security: SOC2 ok, want audit logs for token usage; SSO not critical now.
- Technical asks: sample config for batching (max_batch_size, max_latency_ms), example prefix cache keys for repeated campaign templates, SDK snippet for streaming + function-calling to populate structured fields.

Open items / blockers: pricing table for burst unit rates; explicit rate limit tiers; trial credit top-up for realistic POC traffic (they need ~50K tokens for test). AE notes: send pricing deck + batching guide + Redwood hosted terms. SE to provide POC runbook and sample code by 2026-03-12.
